config.title: Gradients (linear and radial)

intro.title: Gradients (linear and radial)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a colorful webpage that uses CSS gradients to create smooth transitions between colors. You will learn the core concept of defining color blends directly in CSS without using image files. The main technologies involved are the CSS `linear-gradient()` and `radial-gradient()` functions, which allow you to set direction, color stops, and shape. By the end, you'll be able to apply these gradients as backgrounds to style elements with vibrant, custom designs.
intro.usecase: Gradients are essential for creating modern, visually engaging interfaces across web applications. You'll use linear gradients for subtle background transitions in dashboards, data visualization charts, and form headers to guide user attention. Radial gradients create depth in buttons, notification badges, and modal overlays, making elements appear dimensional. These techniques transform flat designs into polished, professional interfaces that enhance user experience in products like analytics platforms, e-commerce sites, and mobile apps.

objectives: Construct a linear gradient background using the linear-gradient() function
Configure gradient direction using keywords and degree values
Manipulate color stops to control gradient transitions
Implement a radial gradient background using the radial-gradient() function
Apply multiple gradients to a single element for layered effects
Integrate gradient backgrounds with other CSS properties in practical layouts
Update existing solid color backgrounds to gradient alternatives

steps.title: Create CSS file and set up basic HTML structure
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and add a basic HTML structure with a container div and heading that will be styled with gradients.
steps.hint: Start with a simple HTML structure that includes a container element and a heading. This will serve as the foundation for applying gradient styles.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create a CSS file and add basic HTML structure */
/* Add your code below this line */
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a CSS file with a basic HTML structure ready for gradient styling.
successCriteria: CSS file contains a .container selector and h1 selector with basic structure
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both a .container selector and h1 selector in your CSS.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Create a CSS file with a .container selector and h1 selector to prepare for gradient styling.

steps.title: Create basic container elements for gradient examples
steps.instruction: Add three div elements with class names 'gradient-box', 'linear-demo', and 'radial-demo' inside the body to serve as containers for gradient examples.
steps.hint: Add three separate <div> tags with the specified class attributes. These will be empty containers that you'll style with gradients in later steps.
steps.analogousExample: /* Similar: creating container elements */
steps.expectedOutcome: Three empty div elements with the specified class names will be created, ready to be styled with gradients.
successCriteria: Three div elements exist with class attributes 'gradient-box', 'linear-demo', and 'radial-demo'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all three div elements with the correct class names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required container elements are missing or incorrect. Please add three div elements with classes 'gradient-box', 'linear-demo', and 'radial-demo'.

steps.title: Style containers with basic dimensions and background
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to give each container a width of 300px, height of 200px, margin of 20px, and a solid background color (choose any color you like).
steps.hint: Use the class selectors .gradient-box, .linear-demo, and .radial-demo to target each element. Set width, height, margin, and background-color properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each container will have consistent dimensions, spacing, and a solid color background, ready for gradient application in later steps.
successCriteria: All three containers have width: 300px, height: 200px, margin: 20px, and a background-color property set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some properties are missing. Ensure all three containers have width, height, margin, and background-color set.
steps.feedbackWrong: The containers are not fully styled. Check that you've added CSS rules for width, height, margin, and background-color to each container class.

steps.title: Apply first linear gradient with two colors
steps.instruction: In the CSS, replace the solid background-color for the .gradient-box element with a linear gradient that transitions from #ff7e5f to #feb47b.
steps.hint: Use the linear-gradient() function as the value for the background property. The gradient should go from the first color to the second color.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .gradient-box element will display a smooth gradient from orange (#ff7e5f) to light orange (#feb47b) instead of a solid gray color.
successCriteria: The .gradient-box selector has a background property (or background-image) with linear-gradient()
The linear-gradient() function contains the colors #ff7e5f and #feb47b
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the linear-gradient() function with both color values (#ff7e5f and #feb47b) in the background property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gradient wasn't applied correctly. Check that you're using linear-gradient() with two color values and that it's set as the background property for .gradient-box.

steps.title: Add direction to linear gradient
steps.instruction: Modify the linear gradient on the .linear-demo element to flow diagonally from top-left to bottom-right using the 'to bottom right' direction.
steps.hint: Update the background property to use linear-gradient(to bottom right, ...) with your chosen colors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The linear gradient on the .linear-demo element should now flow diagonally from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner.
successCriteria: The .linear-demo selector has a background property using linear-gradient with 'to bottom right' direction and two colors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've used 'to bottom right' in the linear-gradient() function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gradient direction isn't correct. Make sure to use 'to bottom right' in the linear-gradient() function.

steps.title: Create linear gradient with multiple color stops
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named 'multi-stop' that creates a linear gradient with at least three color stops at specific percentages.
steps.hint: Use the background property with linear-gradient() and specify colors with percentages like 'red 0%, orange 50%, yellow 100%'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .multi-stop will be added, creating a linear gradient with three or more color stops at specific percentages.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .multi-stop rule with a linear-gradient() that has at least three color stops with percentage values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your gradient has at least three colors with percentage values specified (e.g., 'red 0%, orange 50%, yellow 100%').
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .multi-stop is missing or doesn't contain a linear gradient with multiple color stops at specific percentages.

steps.title: Apply first radial gradient
steps.instruction: In the .radial-demo rule, replace the background-color with a radial gradient that transitions from blue to green.
steps.hint: Use the radial-gradient() function with two colors, similar to how you used linear-gradient() earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .radial-demo element will display a smooth radial gradient from blue at the center to green at the edges.
successCriteria: The .radial-demo rule contains a background property with radial-gradient(blue, green).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the radial-gradient() function with two colors (blue and green) in the .radial-demo rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .radial-demo element should have a radial gradient. Use the radial-gradient() function with blue and green as the color parameters.

steps.title: Control radial gradient shape and size
steps.instruction: Modify the radial gradient on the .radial-demo element to be a circle shape with a size of farthest-corner.
steps.hint: Add shape and size parameters inside the radial-gradient() function: radial-gradient(circle farthest-corner, ...).
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example: radial gradient with shape and size */
background: radial-gradient(circle closest-side, red, blue);
steps.expectedOutcome: The .radial-demo element will have a radial gradient that forms a perfect circle extending to the farthest corner of the container.
successCriteria: The .radial-demo rule includes a radial-gradient with 'circle' shape and 'farthest-corner' size parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both 'circle' and 'farthest-corner' parameters in the radial-gradient function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The radial gradient still needs shape and size parameters. Try adding 'circle farthest-corner' inside the radial-gradient() function.

steps.title: Position radial gradient center point
steps.instruction: Add a position parameter to the radial gradient for the .radial-demo element to control where the gradient originates. Use the format 'at [position]' with either keywords (like 'top left') or percentages (like '30% 70%').
steps.hint: Modify the background property of .radial-demo to include 'at' followed by your chosen position. For example, 'background: radial-gradient(at top left, red, yellow);' or 'background: radial-gradient(at 30% 70%, red, yellow);'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .radial-demo element will display a radial gradient that originates from a specific point you define, rather than the default center.
successCriteria: The .radial-demo CSS rule includes a radial-gradient with a position parameter using 'at' syntax (e.g., 'at top left' or 'at 30% 70%').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct 'at' syntax for positioning (e.g., 'at top left' or 'at 30% 70%'). Check that your radial-gradient includes both colors and position.
steps.feedbackWrong: The radial gradient position wasn't added correctly. Remember to modify the .radial-demo rule to include a radial-gradient with 'at' positioning syntax.

steps.title: Create repeating gradients
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named 'repeating-demo' that creates a repeating linear gradient pattern using the repeating-linear-gradient() function with color stop intervals.
steps.hint: Use the repeating-linear-gradient() function with at least three colors and specify color stop positions to create a striped pattern.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for the 'repeating-demo' class will be added, creating a striped pattern using repeating-linear-gradient() with color stop intervals.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a rule for .repeating-demo that uses repeating-linear-gradient() with at least three colors and specified color stop positions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a repeating gradient, but check that you're using the repeating-linear-gradient() function (not regular linear-gradient) and have specified color stop positions to create the repeating pattern.
steps.feedbackWrong: The repeating gradient wasn't created correctly. Make sure you're adding a new CSS rule for .repeating-demo that uses the repeating-linear-gradient() function with color stop intervals.
